name: Military rule: Murtala and Obasanjo

summary.text: Murtala Muhammed overthrew Gowon in 1975 and replaced every governor. In February 1976 he created seven more states (nineteen in all) and chose Abuja as the new capital. He was killed in a failed coup that month, and his deputy Olusegun Obasanjo handed power to an elected government in 1979. Most governors were posted to states other than their own: a Tiv officer ran Anambra, an Efik officer Ondo, and Igbo officers Lagos and Niger.

federal.text: A Kano-born Northern officer, then a Yoruba officer, led the federal military government.

leaders.name: Murtala Muhammed
leaders.title: Head of State
leaders.groupNote: Born in Kano. Wikipedia traces his father’s line to the Fulani Genawa clan and his mother to the Kanuri and Fulani Jobawa clan. He is often called Hausa, and Kperogi traces his father’s line to northern Edo.

units.name: Federal Capital Territory

reviewNotes: Ethnic attributions follow the cited biographies. Where a biography gives only a birthplace, the people is inferred from it and marked medium; where even that is unclear, the people is shown as “Not recorded”.
The 1976 borders are drawn from today’s LGAs. Kogi is split between Kwara (the old Kabba Province) and Benue (the Igala LGAs). Ebonyi is split between Anambra (Abakaliki) and Imo (Afikpo).
Governors of the twelve states appointed by Murtala in July 1975 are listed under the new state that kept their capital (for example, Ochefu of East Central State under Anambra).

coups.name: Gowon overthrown

fell.name: Yakubu Gowon
fell.role: Head of State, abroad at the OAU summit in Kampala

plotters.name: Joseph Nanven Garba
plotters.role: an insider, who announced the coup

coups.text: Junior officers tired of Gowon’s delays in returning to civilian rule overthrew him while he was at the OAU summit in Kampala. Garba, an insider, kept it bloodless. Murtala, the July 1966 mastermind, became head of state, with Obasanjo as deputy.

moments.title: The broadcast
moments.text: Colonel Joseph Garba announces the coup on Radio Nigeria. Gowon, in Kampala, does not return.

coups.name: Dimka’s coup attempt

plotters.name: Bukar Suka Dimka
plotters.groupNote: His Wikipedia biography does not name his people.

killed.name: Joseph Gomwalk
killed.role: former Governor of Benue-Plateau, executed for links to the plot

coups.text: Dimka’s men ambushed Murtala’s car in Ikoyi traffic and killed him, but the coup was crushed within hours. Dimka named the deposed Gowon in his testimony; Gowon’s fellow Ngas, the former governor Gomwalk, was among those executed. Obasanjo, a Yoruba, took over and handed power to an elected government in 1979.

moments.title: Murtala ambushed
moments.text: Dimka, Major Rabo, Captain Parwang and Lieutenant Seri ambush Murtala’s Mercedes in Ikoyi on its way to Dodan Barracks and kill him and his aide.

moments.title: Dimka on the radio
moments.text: Dimka broadcasts from Radio Nigeria; loyal troops crush the coup within hours and he flees.

moments.title: Dimka caught
moments.text: After a three-week manhunt Dimka is arrested near Abakaliki.

moments.title: The executions
moments.text: Dimka and six co-conspirators are shot after a court martial; Gomwalk is among the condemned.
